engine: markdown
title: "Scripts"
---

```{term}
#| include: false
rush run -o mtcars.csv 'mtcars'
```

Every `rush` command writes a small R script and runs it. With `--dry-run`
(`-n`), `rush` prints that script instead, so you can save it, edit it, and run
it again later.

## Saving a script

The script that `--dry-run` prints is a complete, self-contained
[`ir`](https://r-lib.github.io/ir/) script. Redirect it to a file:

```{term}
rush run --dry-run 'dplyr::filter(df, hp > 200)' mtcars.csv > analysis.R
cat analysis.R
```

The `#|` frontmatter at the top declares the packages the script needs. That
includes `rush` itself, which the script refers to on GitHub
(`github::jeroenjanssens/rush`), pinned to the commit or release that
generated it, so the script keeps working when `rush` changes.

## Running a script

Run it with `ir run`. `ir` installs any missing packages, so the script needs
nothing but `ir` on the machine that runs it:

```{term}
ir run analysis.R
```

The `#!/usr/bin/env -S ir run` line at the top also makes the file
executable (`chmod +x analysis.R && ./analysis.R`). This is handy for
tweaking: dump a `rush` one-liner to a file, edit the generated R to do
something `rush` doesn't express directly, and run it later.

## Scripts without rush

The script above calls helper functions from `rush`, such as `rush::read()`,
which keeps it short. Add `--no-rush` (`-R`) for a script with all of that
code inlined, which doesn't need `rush` at all:

```{term}
rush run -n -R 'dplyr::filter(df, hp > 200)' mtcars.csv > standalone.R
wc -l analysis.R standalone.R
```

The script is longer, but it only uses common packages such as readr, and it
runs the same way:

```{term}
ir run standalone.R
```

## Formatting with air

If the [air](https://posit-dev.github.io/air/) formatter is on your `PATH`,
`rush` runs the `--dry-run` output through it, so the printed script is neatly
formatted and ready to save. This affects only what `--dry-run` shows; the
script that actually runs is never reformatted.

## Running without `ir`

By default `rush` runs each script with `ir`, which installs the packages
declared in the frontmatter when needed. If you would rather use the packages
already installed in your R library (for speed, to work offline, or in an
environment where dependencies are pinned), pass `--no-ir` (`-I`), and `rush`
runs the script with plain `Rscript` instead:

```{term}
rush run --no-ir '6 * 7'
```

In this mode the `#|` frontmatter is left as inert comments and nothing is
installed, so every package the script needs must already be present. The
generated script itself is unchanged, so the same file still runs under `ir`
later.

```{term}
#| include: false
rm -f mtcars.csv analysis.R standalone.R
```
